stories.title: Fish Stocks Thrive Thanks to This Pink Seaweed and Locals Who Protected It
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: Ten years ago, a Scottish island community fought to ban industrial scallop dredging that was tearing up the seabed. That ban protected rare pink 'maerl' beds, a kind of living seaweed that acts like a nursery for baby fish and shellfish. Now, a decade later, islanders are celebrating as fish stocks have bounced back and the seabed is flourishing again. Locals call it the most amazing thing to happen to their waters. It's a real proof that protecting the sea actually pays off.
stories.why_good: A real, decade-long conservation ban has produced measurable, lasting recovery of marine life, directly improving both the ecosystem and local fishing livelihoods.
